production.note: US model years 2021-2023 for this standard 591 hp car. Start: Audi of America, 16 Sep 2020: 'a trio of 2021 RS models are now on sale to customers in the U.S. - the highly anticipated RS 6 Avant, the RS 7, and the first RS-SUV, the RS Q8'. End year is provisional and rests on Kelley Blue Book (database): 2023 lists 'RS 7 Sedan 4D', '591 @ 6000 RPM' (kbb-rs-7-2023); 2024 lists only 'RS 7 performance Sedan 4D', '621 @ 6000 RPM' (kbb-rs-7-2024). The RS 7 performance (621 hp) is a separate variant.

body.note: Audi calls it a 'five-door coupe' (a four-door liftback, sold as the Sportback); Kelley Blue Book lists 'RS 7 Sedan 4D' and Cars.com '4dr Car'. Recorded as Sedan.

displacementL.note: Audi: '4.0-liter TFSI'. Cars.com: 'Displacement 4.0 L/244' (carscom-rs-7-2021). The cc figure was not on a page opened for this car (the same 4.0 TFSI is 3,996 cc in Audi's RS 6/RS Q8 data).

fuel.note: 48-volt mild hybrid, so Gasoline per the data guide. Cars.com: 'Twin Turbo Gas/Electric V-8', 'Gasoline/Mild Electric Hybrid'.

transmission.note: Cars.com: 'Transmission Options 8-Speed A/T' (tiptronic torque-converter automatic). Database source; Audi of America's release does not name the gearbox.

powerHp.note: Quote: "The five-door coupe is equipped with a 4.0-liter TFSI® bi-turbo V8 that generates 591 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque." The later RS 7 performance (621 hp) is a separate variant.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: spec databases. 2021 US RS 7, single configuration. Cars.com quote: "Base Curb Weight 4,938 lbs". Kelley Blue Book (kbb-rs-7-2021) agrees: "Curb Weight 4938 pounds". Two databases agree; no Audi of America or major magazine figure was found. Audi's current US page gives 4,916 lb only for the 2026 RS 7 performance, a different variant.

sources.title: Trio of RS models - 2021 RS 6 Avant, RS 7 and Audi RS Q8 - on sale now

provisionalNote: Weight rests on Cars.com and Kelley Blue Book (databases, both 4,938 lb); an Audi of America specification sheet or a major magazine's specification panel would replace it. The last US model year (2023), the drivetrain and the transmission also rest on databases (Cars.com, Kelley Blue Book); an Audi of America model-year release or spec sheet would replace them.
